title: Telescopic cascode OTA
description: A single-branch telescopic cascode: an input pair, an input (NMOS) cascode, a load (PMOS) cascode, and a load mirror stacked between the rails, all carrying half the tail current, plus the tail source. Cascoding multiplies each side's output resistance by the cascode intrinsic gain, so $A_v = g_{m,in} * R_{out}$ with $R_{out}$ = par(NMOS side, PMOS side) and each side's $R_{out} \approx A_{v0,casc} / g_{ds}$ of the device it cascodes. That is the topology's headline: the highest single-stage gain per unit current, bought with output-swing headroom — the four stacked $V_{dsat}$ plus the tail eat the rail. The stack is parameterized by its NODES, not by per-device drops: the tail node is pinned so the produced $CM_{in}$ equals $CM_{dc}$, and the two internal nodes $V_a$ (input drain / NMOS-cascode source) and $V_b$ (mirror drain / PMOS-cascode source) are choice params. Every device $V_{DS}$ is then a subtraction between adjacent nodes and every source-above-bulk device carries its true body bias — the drops sum to the rail by construction, so there is no consistency guardrail to retune. The cascode-pole and settling behaviour is estimate-grade; sim owns sign-off.

params.name: vn_target
params.note: input-referred thermal density budget; the gamma-model total (pair plus load mirror) lands near 16 nV/rtHz at the default currents, so this leaves real headroom

params.name: vos_target
params.note: input offset budget, 1 sigma; half-micron devices at these currents put the Pelgrom spread near 6.5 mV with a generic coefficient — shrinking this budget is what forces area

params.name: swing_target
params.note: required single-ended output swing (peak) about the output DC — the telescopic's scarcest resource; the swing row computes what the placed nodes leave

params.name: CM_dc
params.note: the input common mode the application presents. The engine places the tail node so the sheet sits exactly here; sweep it to trace the common-mode axis. The slider stops where the stack does: with V_a holding the pair's drain low, the tail node cannot climb past the bracket and the topology genuinely cannot take a higher CM — the telescopic's known input-range ceiling

params.name: V_tail
params.note: the tail node — the pair's source. Solved rather than set: bisected between min and max (the BRACKET) until the produced common mode equals CM_dc. The max must stay far enough below V_a for the pair to size at the top end — the input-sat guardrail owns saturation; the bracket only has to keep both ends on the table

params.name: V_a
params.note: the NMOS-side internal node: input drain and input-cascode source. Set by the cascode gate bias in silicon; here a direct choice — the input vds is V_a - V_tail and the cascode's is V_out_dc - V_a, by construction

params.name: V_b
params.note: the PMOS-side internal node: mirror drain and load-cascode source. The mirror vds is VDD - V_b and the cascode's is V_b - V_out_dc, by construction

params.name: V_out_dc
params.note: output DC level; the NMOS drops below it and the PMOS drops above it must each close the rail

params.name: sign_p
params.note: vds sign convention of the PMOS-side tables: +1 for an N-style axis, -1 for a signed-PMOS axis

params.name: gm_id_in
params.note: input-pair inversion: sets gm per current and the input-referred noise

params.name: gm_id_casc
params.note: cascode-device inversion: higher gm/ID lifts the cascode gain av0_casc but costs vdsat headroom

params.name: gm_id_mir
params.note: load-mirror inversion: lower gm/ID adds less noise and offset

doc.title: Input-pair device
doc.description: Half-circuit input device at half the tail current; its ro sets the NMOS-side cascoded output resistance. Its source sits at the tail node (its body bias) and its drain at V_a.

doc.title: Input (NMOS) cascode
doc.description: Cascodes the input device; its intrinsic gain av0 multiplies the input ro to set the NMOS-side Rout. Its source stands on the internal node V_a, so that is its body bias.

doc.title: Load (PMOS) cascode
doc.description: Cascodes the load mirror; its intrinsic gain av0 multiplies the mirror ro to set the PMOS-side Rout. Its source stands on the internal node V_b, below the bulk at VDD, so its body bias is VDD - V_b (the PMOS tables' vsb axis carries that magnitude).

doc.title: Load mirror device
doc.description: One side of the PMOS load mirror at half the tail current; its ro (cascoded by casc_p) sets the PMOS-side output resistance.

doc.title: Tail current source
doc.description: Carries the full bias current; its vdsat is the extra headroom below the input source node.

rows.name: CM_in
rows.note: the input common mode this bias produces — an OUTPUT here, not a setting; rises monotonically with the tail node, so the pin is a well-posed bisection

rows.name: tail_headroom
rows.note: how far the tail node sits above the tail device's saturation edge — exact, because the tail node is the variable rather than something inferred from a common mode

rows.name: Rout_n
rows.note: NMOS-side output resistance: input ro boosted by the input-cascode intrinsic gain

rows.name: Rout_p
rows.note: PMOS-side output resistance: mirror ro boosted by the load-cascode intrinsic gain

rows.name: Rout
rows.note: the two cascoded sides in parallel

rows.name: vn_in
rows.note: input pair plus the load mirror's own density referred by gm_mir/gm_in; the cascodes add little (they carry the same current at low gm relative to the pair)

rows.name: vos
rows.expr: sqrt(pelgrom_vos(avt, abeta, in__W, L_in, gm_id_in)^2 + (pelgrom_vos(avt, abeta, mir__W, L_mir, gm_id_mir)*mir__gm/in__gm)^2)
rows.note: input-pair offset plus the load mirror's offset referred by the gm ratio

rows.name: swing
rows.note: peak-to-peak output swing the PLACED nodes actually leave, symmetric about the output DC: the output can fall to V_a plus the NMOS cascode's vdsat and rise to V_b minus the PMOS cascode's — the idealized stacked-vdsat budget read ~3x optimistic once the nodes were explicit. Push V_a down and V_b up to widen it

rules.note: below this the tail source drops out of saturation and the bias current collapses; the mechanism behind the low end of the common-mode range
the stacked headroom must leave at least the peak-to-peak output swing

the input device's node placement: V_a must sit at least a vdsat above the tail node. The drops sum to the rail by construction now — what is left to check is that each node leaves its device saturated
the input cascode's node placement: the output DC must sit at least a vdsat above V_a
the load cascode's node placement: V_b must sit at least a vdsat above the output DC
the load mirror's node placement: V_b must leave the mirror at least a vdsat below VDD
